key_insight: Introduce a hierarchical, self-supervised representation of human movement where low-level "Action Atoms" (atomic joint motions) compose into higher-level "Action Motifs" that recur across different actions, learned via a nested latent Transformer (A4Mer). This captures compositionality and shared movement patterns across actions.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of discovering compact, interpretable, and transferable sub-movement structures from pose sequences without labels, enabling better modeling of compositional human behavior.
method: Define two-level hierarchy: Action Atoms (atomic joint movements) and Action Motifs (temporal compositions of atoms) to represent motions compositionally.
Train A4Mer, a nested latent Transformer, on human pose sequences in a self-supervised manner to learn atoms and motifs jointly from data.
Use the hierarchical latent codes for downstream tasks (e.g., recognition, retrieval, synthesis) and to reveal motif sharing across different actions.
impact: Provides a compact, interpretable motion representation that improves transferability and sample efficiency for downstream tasks (action recognition, motion synthesis, few-shot learning), while enabling analysis of shared sub-movements across actions.
visual_elements: Hierarchy diagram: stack showing Joint -> Action Atoms -> Action Motifs -> Full Action with arrows indicating composition
Timeline visualization: pose sequence segmented into atoms and motifs (color-coded) mapped to the hierarchy
Latent-space clustering: 2D projection showing motifs shared across different labeled actions
Application thumbnail grid: icons illustrating downstream uses (recognition, retrieval, synthesis, transfer)
paper_title: Action Motifs: Self-Supervised Hierarchical Representation of Human Body Movements
paper_authors: Genki Kinoshita, Shu Nakamura, Ryo Kawahara, Shohei Nobuhara, Yasutomo Kawanishi
